$comment: Decisions that govern scripts/replications/migrate-article-media.mjs. Three kinds of fact live here, none of them derivable from src/data/config/articleMediaCuration.json alone: the owner rulings that override the curation file, the near-duplicates verified against live production, and the canonical Convex storage id behind each article embed. Regenerate storageIds only by re-resolving against production; see the script header.

uploads.$comment: Bytes that no Convex object holds yet. Every row the first pass inserted pointed at a storage object that already existed; these five were recovered from the live web on 2026-08-11 and have to be uploaded before a row can reference them. `path` is relative to --uploads-dir. `sha256` is the base64 sha-256 of the exact reviewed bytes and is checked before the upload, so a re-fetched or substituted file fails closed instead of quietly becoming the published asset. `contentType` is re-derived from the file's own container signature at run time and must agree with the value here — a WebP served as image/jpeg downloads instead of rendering, and the extension is not evidence.

a005-white-wolf-drinking-water.note: 14-frame animated GIF, verified with ffprobe. The filename records the three ids the recovery pass was chasing at once; only A005/A006 are this asset. A038 is the Dissociative Hole teaching slide, which already has a Convex object and is filed separately.

variantGroups.$comment: Two Convex objects, one work, and a choice that cannot be made from the metadata. Unlike the same-object collapse the batch already performs, these differ in bytes, so nothing automatic can tell which copy should be the published one.
variantGroups.name: lsd-sunflower
variantGroups.reason: Owner ruling: two embeds of one photograph, take the wider crop. Measured against production on 2026-08-11 there is no wider crop — both objects are the same 1982x2642 framing (24x24 greyscale rmse 0.0019, confirmed by eye side by side). With the crops equal the ruling's intent falls to the better copy, which is A073 at 511,812 bytes against A072's 339,074: same pixels, less JPEG compression.

heldGroups.name: audio
heldGroups.reason: Owner ruling 6, reaffirmed in round 2: replications.type accepts audio but no surface renders it, and isPublishableReplication withholds it deliberately. The five distinct files behind these ids all serve HTTP 200 from public/audio/, so this is a wait for a player rather than a loss. A054 left this group in round 2 — the hunt for it finished and found nothing, so it is now recorded as dead.

deadAssetsLeftDead.$comment: Nothing survives to file. Owner ruling 5 said do not chase dead assets and do not substitute anything, and round 2's recovery pass settled which of them were truly gone. A054 (/audio/deliriant audio.mp3) and S002 (the deliriants.jpg page hero) each survived two independent passes with nothing found; A085 is a filename whose object 404s. A021, A028, A029, A035 and A037 left this list in round 2 because the recovery pass actually found them — A021 is now promoted above, and the other four are dropped on their merits rather than for being missing.

$resolved-2026-09-04.$comment: Round 3 emptied two of these three. The searches behind them were correct about the public web and wrong about what the owner already held: the bytes were in the owner's own PsychonautWiki mirror (psychonautwiki.rip), which no earlier pass had queried. Recorded here because 'searched twice, found nothing' was about to become a permanent ruling on assets that exist. Digests, dimensions and sources are in recovery/batch3/manifest.json; both are now published to the R2 media bucket.
$resolved-2026-09-04.A085: Recovered from the mirror under the same filename, 326x49 animated GIF, 163836 bytes. Owner approved shipping the audited batch on 2026-09-05. The lucid-dreaming body and AST now reference the recovered R2 object; production readback verified the replacement.
$resolved-2026-09-04.S002: Recovered from the mirror at 750x1127, and then superseded: the artist has a later rendition of the same composition published on this site as replication 700mg-of-dph-stas-constantine (1536x2048). The deliriant hero points at the artist's own work; the archive copy is kept only as the record of what the Effect Index page served.
$resolved-2026-09-04.A054: Still dead. No copy of /audio/deliriant audio.mp3 in the mirror or anywhere else searched.

droppedAssets.$comment: Round 2. An asset that exists and is still not filed. Distinct from deadAssetsLeftDead, where there is nothing to file: each of these was recovered or is live, and the owner ruled it out on its merits. Recorded so a later pass does not read the absence of a row as an oversight and re-open it.

droppedAssets.name: wrong-image-for-the-caption
droppedAssets.reason: The caption promises a symbolic representation of time distortion; the asset is a photograph of two sandalled feet on grass, mirrored into a symmetrical field. The embed is wrong, not the asset. Fix the article rather than filing the mismatch as a credited row.

artistCorrections.$comment: The curation entry's own evidence disowns its artist_name: 'The stored artist Alice is the fictional character and must not become a contributor profile; the caption's Alice by Lewis Caroll names the author, not the illustrator. The real credit is Sir John Tenniel, public domain.' The replacement is taken verbatim from the same entry's attribution field, not invented.
artistCorrections.reason: Alice is the character depicted, not the engraver. Filing her as the artist would mint a contributor profile for a fictional person.

recoverableLater.$comment: What the round-2 recovery pass settled, kept as the record of why nothing here is outstanding. The script no longer only reuses existing Convex objects — see `uploads` above — so a recovered asset is migrated by this script rather than by a separate upload step. It stays re-runnable: a slug already in production is skipped before its bytes are ever read, so a second run uploads nothing and inserts nothing.

A021 and S001 — RECOVERED and migrated. A Wayback capture of a dead gfycat id and a PsychonautWiki copy of the Effect Index page hero.

A004 UV mandala and A011 Patterning clouds — RECOVERED and then NOT migrated. Each turned out to be a work production already carries (uv-mandala-symmetric-vision and lsd-on-a-cloudy-day-jumproper); see verifiedDuplicates. Both recovered copies are larger than the rows' current MP4s, so replacing those rows' assets is a separate, optional job — an upgrade, not a missing row. Neither was findable before the recovery pass: the first pass's pixel sweep covered image rows, and a dead asset has no pixels to sweep.

A054 and S002 — searched twice, found nothing. Recorded in deadAssetsLeftDead.
